Priya S: onboarding run for magnet-lite-32k-int8 completed. seeing a tiled-kv checksum delta around token 30112 -> downstream token alignment shifts. filing initial notes here.
Luca V: can you paste the exact CLI and flags used?
Priya S: ran with:
```
./ci/longctx_harness --model magnet-lite-32k --quant int8-channelwise --ropescale rescale2 --prefill_stride 128 --kv-checksum 1024 --capture-kv --job magnet-20260319-01
```
Priya S: excerpt from runtime-log:
```
[2026-03-19T07:02:18Z] KV-CHECKSUM(tile=29,start=29696,len=1024)=0x5a3c9f
[2026-03-19T07:02:18Z] KV-CHECKSUM_DECOMP(tile=29,dequanted)=0x5a3c9f
[2026-03-19T07:02:18Z] KV-CHECKSUM(runtime-int8,tile=30)=0x4f7aa1
[2026-03-19T07:02:18Z] DIFF: first-mismatch tile=30 offset=116 global-token=30112
[2026-03-19T07:02:18Z] INFER(INT8): token=30113 predicted="agreement" prob=0.73
[2026-03-19T07:02:18Z] INFER(FP16): token=30113 predicted="agreement." prob=0.89
```
Mia Nguyen: interesting, mismatch is exactly at tile boundary. did you see the same tile reorder issue that INFRA-6214 flagged last week?
Priya S: infra team said no memcopy reorder for the host that ran this job (checked), but i'm still suspicious about shard-join ordering when prefill stride 128 != tile size 1024.
Jordan M: quick thought: if the dequantization scale is computed per-shard instead of global, small per-shard rounding could accumulate and flip tokens at the boundary.
Luca V: can you re-run with `--quant-scale-mode global` and `--rotary-interpolate true` to normalize scaling across shards?
Priya S: running that next. job magnet-20260319-02.
ci-bot: job magnet-20260319-01 artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/magnet-20260319-01/logs.tar.gz uploaded.
Priya S: re-run results (quick): checksum diff count drops from 4 -> 0 across 8/8 tiles when using global scale + rotary-interpolate. however we see a throughput regression ~5% and slight increase in memory by ~120MB.
Mia Nguyen: good signal that quant-scale sharding might be root cause. i'd still like a cross-check: run hybrid quantization (layers 0..10 int8, rest fp16) to see if mismatch persists. if it disappears, then rounding cascade hypothesis strengthened.
Priya S: hybrid run (magnet-20260319-03) shows one residual mismatch in tile 31 but token alignment preserved. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-19T08:45:02Z] KV-CHECKSUM(tile=31)=0x7c1e22
[2026-03-19T08:45:02Z] DIFF: tile=31 offset=12 global-token=30760 -> soft-delta discovered, but downstream generation identical for first 64 tokens
```
Jordan M: that suggests mismatch doesn't always cascade into generation divergence. could be low-entropy tokens at that position. run pairwise perplexity on windowed segments across the legal corpus.
Luca V: I'll write a small script to compute per-window KL(fp16||int8) and surface spikes. PR incoming to tools: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/190
Priya S: opened ticket ML-9327 to add `--quant-scale-mode` to onboarding checklist for 32k models and capture perf cost. linking artifacts.
ci-bot: job magnet-20260319-02 completed, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/magnet-20260319-02/
Mia Nguyen: ops note: if global-scale fixes correctness, we might still want to keep per-shard scaling for latency-sensitive hosted profiles. recommend a short experiment: global-scale on canary dedicated pool and measure tail latency.
Priya S: agreed. scheduling canary run and perf sweep. will report back with KL heatmap and tile checksums.
Jordan M: if we decide to keep per-shard scale for latency, at least add a rollback-safe runtime flag to enable checksum-only validation on suspect requests.
Priya S: putting that in ML-9327. thanks all. :rocket:
